assumptions: The removers are control_space_remove.remove(ledger, probe, identity, record, action, free, keep, run, proc) and tool(...), which gives the same in the form rule 7 calls. Nothing calls them yet: Signal's carry out and the outcome it writes are VELDO-0301. A remover writes nothing to the ledger.

NO WORK LOST, as built here. The spec's History says the keep step is added inside the worktree and private repository removers by VELDO-0345. Until then those two removers do not run without it: keep(identity, record) is a parameter, and with none, or any answer but {ok: True}, the item is deferred keep_failed and nothing is touched. This is beyond the four criteria and is built so that no path of this module can remove commits unrecorded; it has its own row and two falsifiers. What the keeper does and the check of the keep record are VELDO-0345.

Not built here, because each saves first and belongs to a later ticket: the discard remover (VELDO-0318, the one forced removal), the review scratch remover (VELDO-0336) and the removal of evidence files a copy holds (remove_held). So AC3's exception for the discard remover has nothing to except yet: no command of this module carries a force option. Mark a branch contained is a ledger write and is not a remover.

A refusal reaches Signal as rule 7's found.said. The rules name every tool refusal remove_refused (control_space_signal.DEFERRAL, not in this ticket's footprint); the remover's own answer names the deferral it means (remove_refused, in_use, keep_failed) in said.deferral and said.reason. Review finding 6: no code of Signal or of the ledger was changed. Since the re-review it is bound by criteria and not by a History note: VELDO-0301 AC5 (the remover's deferral passed through; an answer with left_at keeps the item removing) and VELDO-0345 AC6 (the ledger accepts the three deferrals for a removing item). Until both are built a keep_failed or in_use refusal of a removing item would be recorded as remove_refused; nothing calls the removers yet.

REVIEW FIX, finding 4. The folder remover now holds the line by itself: the walk that measures the folder before the first delete stops on any folder that is a git repository or holds one, and the folder is put back. An agent repository and a worktree may hold their own and no other. The clean clone exception of design 0.1 and rule 6's own-folder look are still VELDO-0347 (its History says the remover refuses until then).

free(pool record) is given, as admission is given it; reading free space from a filesystem or an engine is VELDO-0316. With no reader, or a reading that fails before the removal, nothing is removed. In the suite the reader is a stand-in: the host pool answers a fixed capacity minus the measured size of the fixture folders, the engine image pool answers the stand-in engine's figure, so freed can be compared exactly.

The container engine is a stand-in function given as the client runner: it keeps containers, images, volumes and networks in memory and refuses what an engine refuses. No container engine was asked anything, so the engines' real refusal texts and the real effect of image rm on a last tag (the engine deletes the image with it) are not measured here; they are VELDO-0306's to check on both engines.

bytes for a volume is measured only where the engine names a folder this user can read; otherwise the ledger's last measurement, named as that, or None. bytes for a folder counts blocks on disk, a file with several names once.

A mount point is refused by os.path.ismount; the row proves the helper on /proc and the refusal with the helper replaced for one folder, because the suite cannot mount. A filesystem mounted inside the folder stops the measurement before any delete (the device of every directory is compared); that stop and a failing delete are driven in the suite by replacing the module's delete function, not by a real failure.
drop_caches removes the declared sub-folders one by one. When a later one refuses, the earlier ones are gone; they are caches by the project's own declaration.
One command of a tool may run for an hour (SECONDS). A git remove that is killed at that bound can leave a worktree partly removed; that is reconcile's case (design 0.2), not handled here.
The process table of the rows is a fixture folder, because this host's table holds processes this user may not read and they count as use (design section 7).

REVIEW FIX, finding 7 (VELDO-0299's module, changed with this fix on the lead's instruction): the probes' git goes through the Git boundary, scripts/check_git_boundary.py allows control_space_probe.py as a funnel (that file is not a protected path in .veldo/policy.yaml) and passes for the whole tree, so suite 50's row git-boundary/no-private-git-invocations is no longer expected red for this reason. Suite 50_git_environment was run alone after the fix: 30 checks passed, 0 failed. The remover's own runner sends a git vector it is handed through the boundary as well.

Because git runs in the Git boundary's isolated profile, a file that only a personal global excludes file ignores is an untracked file to git's worktree remove, and git refuses. That is the direction design 0.1 asks for.
python3 scripts/check_first_use.py was started once by mistake during the fast checks (it is a heavy check) and was stopped; no result of it is claimed.

REVIEW FIX, the keep step's answer. keep(identity, record) must answer {ok: True, tips, snapshot}: tips is what control_space_remove.tips(path, kind) read in the item, snapshot is {files: {relative path: {mode, sha256}}}. The keeper is VELDO-0345 and is not built; its History has this contract. In the suite the keeper is a stand-in that calls tips itself and names the snapshot the row gives it.

REVIEW FIX, what is build output to the last look: an ignored FOLDER whose rule git traces (check-ignore) to a .gitignore that is tracked in that work tree, or whose name matches a build_output pattern the owning project declares. Every other ignored path is work, a loose ignored file whatever rule covers it (design 0.1). The cost is the design's: a worktree with loose ignored files (a local settings file, object files beside sources) waits until a keep step saves them. An empty ignored folder is no work.

REVIEW FIX, deferrals chosen where the review left a choice: work the keep step did not save, and a tip it did not record, are keep_failed; a user under the marked name is in_use; a repository in the folder, a link or .. in the path and git's own refusals are remove_refused.

What the last look does not close (design 0.9 names it): a process that finds the marked name and writes there between the last look and git's one remove command. The rename has no no-replace flag from the standard library: an EMPTY folder that appears at the marked name between the check and the rename is replaced.

A worktree on a branch with no commit yet, or whose log git cannot walk, is deferred keep_failed (the tips cannot be read) and stays. A worktree removal killed between git's move and git's remove leaves the whole worktree under its marked name with git's record pointing there; finding it is reconcile's (VELDO-0315 AC2, whose History names left, marked and unmarked). Nothing calls left yet.

RE-REVIEW FIX, finding D (the first review's finding 9), fixed in code and no longer pointed at VELDO-0341. Each Docker remover has the engine show the object and compares it with the item's record before it asks for any remove: the Id when the locator holds id, and the label com.docker.compose.project when the locator holds compose_project (read from Labels, or from Config.Labels for a container or an image). What this cannot see: an engine gives a volume no Id of its own, so a volume recorded by name alone, with no compose project, has nothing to compare, and the run's own label is not in the item's record. The row uses the stand-in engine, which is given an Id for the volume. The engine has no remove conditional on an Id, so a volume swapped between the show and the remove is not seen.

The design text is not edited by the review fix. Its 6.5 row for a worktree moves it to a marked name only after a Save; the remover now does so at every worktree removal. The spec's History says it. commit and tree above still name the build commit c2902100; the review fix is the commit that carries this bundle.

RE-REVIEW FIX, finding A, a choice made here. The review says a hidden changed file is unsaved (keep_failed) for both kinds and never left to git. For an agent repository it always refuses. For a worktree it is held as an ignored file that is work is held: it refuses unless the keep step's snapshot holds the file with the same mode and digest, in which case it is saved and the worktree goes. A hidden file that is not on disk is not work (nothing of it is only there). A hidden file of another type than the index says, and a gitlink, count as changed. Content is compared by git's own hash-object, so the repository's clean filters apply; the executable bit alone is not compared. One hash-object process is run per hidden file that is on disk.

RE-REVIEW FIX, finding B. Any entry of git worktree list besides the first refuses an agent repository, bare or not, with no exception: no keep step saves a linked worktree's index yet (VELDO-0345's History names it). Through the rule chain rule 6 already refuses such a repository before the remover is reached; the row therefore proves the remover's own refusal by calling it by itself, as the reviewer's repro did. Finding C: adopted is the ledger's own field of the item's record; the row's item is made by the ledger's adopt.

The re-review's last table row is not a finding and is not changed: in a worktree recorded when it was made, a folder a committed rule such as *.local or .vscode/ covers is build output and goes with the worktree (design 0.1, 6.3). The spec's History tells the owner. The residual windows the re-review accepts (a write after the last look by a process that found the marked name) are unchanged. commit and tree above still name the build commit c2902100; the re-review fix is the commit that carries this bundle.
rollback: Revert the change. Removers are called only through Signal, and nothing calls them yet, so without them nothing is removed.
